sign: Houses on stilts. Please don't jump on the walkways.

lines: Tender Agna: The tide brings fresh water in at the stilt-spring. Let your team drink.
Trader Lusk: Dry towels and remedies. The fen gets into everything.
trader.action: shop tonic strong_tonic max_tonic remedy dry_towel wake_bell revival_leaf kin_charm

lines: Boatman Rurik: The Lake Line runs again. Brindlewick, Quillbrook, wherever you've set foot.
Eel-Catcher Gunn: West end by day, east end by evening. The eels move, so do I.
Eel-Catcher Gunn: The eels came back to the stilts. They know when the water's right.
Stilt-Builder Aart: I check the stilts by the gate each morning. One wobble and I know.
Stilt-Builder Aart: No wobble in weeks. The Rift shook more than the storm ever did.
Reed-Cutter Wenna: I cut reeds from dawn to noon and sleep through the evening. Don't tell.
Reed-Cutter Wenna: The reeds grow so fast now I can't keep up. A nice problem.
Lantern Boy Pip: I'm allowed up at night to watch the lanterns on the water. It's my job!
Lantern Boy Pip: The lanterns don't flicker blue anymore. I kind of liked the blue.
Fishwife Hanne: Morning catch here, evening market in Brindlewick. My feet know every plank.
Fishwife Hanne: Folk buy fish again without sniffing it twice. The Rift scared them off the lake.
An old cartographer's stone. A compass rose is cut into it, worn almost smooth.
A bench with a view over the lake. Sit and listen for a while?

lake_hint: An old fen-cutter rows past: "That smooth boulder in Brackwater Fen? Hands put it there, to hide a way."

lines: A fish trap hangs from the jetty, half under water.
A fish trap hangs from the jetty, half under water.
Stilt-Builder Aart: Very funny. Here, coins. Now stand still before you fall in.
